models_evaluated: Bach et al. lung cancer risk prediction model (LCS Decision Precision tool)

links.outcome: Benefit-based lung cancer screening uptake before vs after category-specific encouragement tool
links.effect: Benefit-based LCS OR 1.03 preimplementation vs 1.81 implementation and 1.55 postimplementation; final-month screening probability 24.8% high-benefit vs 15.8% intermediate (difference 9.0 points; 95% CI, 1.6%-16.5%).
links.quote: This association was sustained, and by the final month of the study, the mean (SD) estimated probability of getting screened for a high-benefit person was 24.8% (15.5%) vs 15.8% (11.8%) for a person at intermediate (preference-sensitive) benefit (mean absolute difference, 9.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.6%-16.5%).

unlisted_practices: Prediction-augmented shared decision-making tool that tailors strength of screening encouragement to predicted benefit
Academic detailing and learning sessions to train clinicians on using prediction-augmented decision support
Monitoring for unintended low-value screening after predictive tool implementation
